name: FillMatic
outcome: Turns repetitive test-data entry into a reusable one-click workflow.
description: A Chrome extension that fills real-world web forms with realistic test data in one click, including the controls most autofill tools miss.

highlights: One-click realistic names, emails, addresses, dates, phone numbers, and payment test data
Framework-aware writes keep React and Vue-style controlled inputs in sync
Drives ARIA comboboxes, calendars, switches, sliders, and radio groups like a user would
Rich-text support for ProseMirror, Lexical, Slate, Quill, Trix, and contenteditable
Profiles, Actions, and Recipes turn repeated test flows into reusable workflows
Teach mode records custom interactions as safe declarative steps, with no eval or remote code
Optional on-device AI with Gemini Nano through Chrome's Prompt API refines field maps, while the full heuristic workflow works without it
Fill-only by default: it never submits a form unless you turn that on
details.problem: Realistic form testing breaks down on modern UIs. Controlled React inputs ignore naive value writes, custom selects and date pickers are not real form controls, and checkout fields often mount only after you interact with the page. Testers end up retyping the same data by hand or maintaining brittle scripts.
details.architecture: A Chrome extension split across popup, settings, side panel, and a background service worker. Content scripts own every DOM mutation, one per frame. Fills run through an ordered strategy pipeline: native inputs first, then a DOM quiet-period and a second pass for late-mounted controls, then user Recipes, widget adapters, and editor-aware insertion. A failure on one element is logged and skipped instead of aborting the whole form. Everything lives in chrome.storage.local, with no application backend. The optional side-panel mapper runs Gemini Nano on-device through Chrome's Prompt API, and its output is reviewed and saved as a normal Action, so running an Action never needs the model.
engineering: Failure-isolated pipeline: one broken field never takes down the rest of the form
Deterministic value resolution: Actions and profile rules outrank heuristics, so results are predictable
Privacy by design: no application server, and on-device Gemini Nano means page contents are never transmitted for mapping
Typed, command-scoped messaging between extension contexts, with a repeat-fill that survives reloads
Tested in real Chromium with Playwright, including a real Radix Select, shadow DOM, and iframes
Enforced 90% coverage floors across statements, branches, functions, and lines
Tagged releases are tested, packaged, and published to the Chrome Web Store through CI

name: Polychat
outcome: Keeps multi-provider workflows and conversation context in one private workspace.
description: A local-first AI workspace for chat, images, and multilingual work, with an encrypted bring-your-own-key vault.

highlights: Switch between Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, and DeepSeek in one workspace
Tune each thread: model, assistant profile, response language, and multi-turn context
Stream rich Markdown with tables, syntax-highlighted code, copy actions, and file downloads
Generate images and attach images or documents (PDF, DOCX, CSV, JSON and more) as context
Threads, messages, images, and preferences stay in your browser, not on a server
Encrypted BYOK vault with optional passkey unlock on supported devices
Voice input, speech playback, light, dark, and system themes, and layouts from desktop to mobile
Per-message and per-thread token counts when you want to see usage
details.problem: Polychat started as a tool I needed. I use it myself to try different models sometimes, especially through OpenRouter, and I keep adding the features as required. Using several AI providers usually means juggling separate tools, settings, and chat histories, and handing your conversations and API keys to yet another service. Polychat puts the providers in one place and keeps the data on your device.
details.architecture: A React 19 and React Router 7 SPA with Jotai state and a TipTap composer. Threads, images, and the key vault persist locally in IndexedDB. A small Hono API on AWS Lambda authenticates Clerk JWTs and streams chat as newline-delimited JSON through the Vercel AI SDK, so tokens appear as they arrive. In production, requests go through a Cloudflare Pages proxy that adds a shared secret the Lambda requires. Model metadata and types are shared through a workspace package.
engineering: Envelope encryption: provider keys are sealed with a random AES-GCM vault key
The vault key is wrapped by a PBKDF2-SHA-256 passphrase key (600,000 iterations)
Optional WebAuthn PRF device unlock, with passphrase recovery as the fallback
The server never stores the vault or its passphrase
Streaming end to end, from the provider through Lambda to the UI
Type-safe model catalog: provider-compatible model IDs derived from the AI SDK types
Locked-down API: Clerk JWT checks with an authorized-parties allowlist, plus a proxy secret in production
